The user asks: "I need to re-run this import today and I'm worried about creating duplicates of the rows that already succeeded — can you confirm before I run it?" This is about import duplicates. The policy excerpts provide guidance: If correction was to email address or identifier used for matching, importer can't recognize same row, safest is to remove already-succeeded rows from corrected file before re-running. Also, a row that succeeded and is present unchanged in corrected file will be recognized as same record and updated rather than duplicated, as long as matching field wasn't corrected. Also, fix flagged rows and re-run import against just those rows, rather than whole file, avoids re-processing rows that already succeeded.

Thus we can answer: If you haven't changed the matching field (email/identifier), you can include unchanged rows and they will be updated not duplicated. If you changed matching field, you need to remove succeeded rows from file. Also you can re-run only the rows that failed. So confirm that duplicates won't happen if matching field unchanged. Provide guidance.
